S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms within three months of an identifiable stressor, with distress that is out of proportion to the stressor or associated with significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The presentation can include anxious, depressed, or mixed mood changes, as well as maladaptive behaviors, but does not meet full criteria for another specific mental disorder and is not merely an exacerbation of a preexisting condition. Symptoms typically resolve within six months after the stressor or its consequences have ended, though it can become chronic if the stressor persists. It is differentiated from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from disorders such as major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder by its time-limited course and clear temporal relationship to a specific stressor.

patient.personality: Tim is an energetic, improvisational caregiver who thrives on spontaneity, social connection, and hands-on activities but dislikes rigid structure and detailed planning.
patient.stressor: About two months ago, after weeks of ignoring nagging fatigue and shortness of breath, Tim was unexpectedly hospitalized and diagnosed with a chronic cardiac condition that required medication, dietary changes, and limits on physically strenuous activity. For someone used to leading lively group sessions at the senior center, bowling in a league, and hauling lumber for woodworking projects, the abrupt shift to being a "patient" with restrictions felt like a profound blow to his identity and independence. He initially tried to shrug it off with humor and keep up his usual pace, but as his cardiologist warned him about overexertion and his employer temporarily reassigned him to less active duties, he began to feel increasingly cornered by the lifestyle changes and struggled to adjust his day-to-day routines. When his difficulty following medical advice and changes in his reliability at work started to create tension with colleagues and risked his position at the senior center, a supportive supervisor and his primary care physician encouraged him to see a psychiatrist to address how he was coping with the new health limitations.
patient.chief_complaint: Since I found out about this heart issue, I just haven’t been dealing with it well and it’s really messing with how I handle my life and my job.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since they told me about my heart, I swing between wanting to pretend nothing’s wrong—pushing the residents’ wheelchairs too fast, sneaking into the bowling alley for “just a few frames”—and then crashing at home, sitting in my recliner all evening feeling angry, useless, and snapping at people when they remind me of the rules I’m supposed to follow.
